title: Workers start the longest test scopes first and match the host's cores
goal: tests.py orders its loadscope units so the git scenario classes with long class fixtures are handed out first, and chooses its worker count from a measured default instead of one worker per logical CPU.
links: kb/public/python/pytest-xdist.md (loadscope reorder, worksteal, -n auto without psutil, PYTEST_XDIST_AUTO_NUM_WORKERS)
notes: Measured: under loadscope the git scenario classes (100-520 s of class setup each) start 500-1,050 s into the run, and 1,124-1,288 worker-seconds sit idle at the end; --no-loadscope-reorder (file order) gave 1,190 s against 1,106-1,203 s, no gain. Expected saving: 120-160 s of wall time from ordering the heaviest scopes first. -n auto starts 8 workers on this 4-core, 8-thread host because uv.lock has no psutil; the worker-count runs are in the report. Kept as a draft: the operator has not scheduled the test-speed epic EP-hlnsqx4f. Its checks name _tools/perfcheck.py and _tools/test_ids_baseline.txt, which ST-c35i7vjx "A tool proves a test-suite speed-up lost no test" creates, so that story comes first.
